Twelve comments

Jimmy O’Reilly’s

I fell in love with this tune when I heard it played in Kevin Crawford’s “In Good Company,” but I gave up learning it by ear at that time because I had just picked up the instrument. Around a couple of weeks ago I accidentally found one version of this reel was available in Richard Moon’s tune database and arranged it listening to Kevin and Tommy Peoples’ playing. Here is the original the setting.

T: John Naughton’s Favorite
S: “Treoir”
M: 4/4
L: 1/8
R: reel
K: Ador
ABAG EGDE | G2 BG dGBG | ABAG E>G D2 | Beed BA A2 |
ABAG EGDE | G2 BG dGBG | ABAG E>G D2 | gedB BA A2 :|
ageg a2 ba | gede g2 bg | ageg a2 ga | bgga bg g2 |
bg g2 afef | gedB BABd | egfa g3 d | gedB BA A2 :|

Many, many thanks to Will for correcting the details of the ABC.

↳ Posted by slainte on February 3rd, 2003.

Jimmy O’Reilly’s, X:7

Declan Masterson version in End of the Harvest.
Copy and paste from version 6 and update mostly the structure and the transition notes between parts :

Part A is played once only
Part B is played twice

This structure with Part A played once and B part played twice (repeated) is also found in Mary MacNamara and Martin Hayes. A fiddle tutorial form Paul McNevin also use this “A BB” structure.

Kevin Crawford plays the A part twice (and B part twice also)..

↳ Posted by UPipes & harp on April 30th, 2024.

Re: Jimmy O’Reilly’s

My mistake, Martin Hayes plays this reel as a single reel AB AB in the “Lonesome Touch”, and so does Mary MacNamara in “Traditional Music from East Clare”

Thus according to the payer / recording, we have the three ways of playing the reel :
AB AB
AA BB AA BB
A BB A BB

↳ Posted by UPipes & harp on May 5th, 2024.

The original link is thesession.org/tunes/1406
